title: Sundial Analytics SDK & Env Standup — Quickstart + Auth
summary: Intro and quickstart walkthrough of Redwood SDKs (Python + TypeScript), auth patterns (API key vs SSO), sandbox environment setup, basic Optimize recommendations for embeddings and token batching. Agreed next steps: share security pack, provide sandbox creds, run a short latency benchmark, and schedule a follow-up POC-scoping session.
next_steps: Redwood: Send security/compliance packet and SOC2 snapshot (Maya)
Redwood: Provision sandbox org and short-lived API key for Sundial (Ravi)
Customer: Run 1-hour latency benchmark and share traces (Omar)
Schedule POC scoping call w/ infra and product — target week of 6/23 (all)
Share sample prompt set for Optimize evals (Laura)
action_items: Maya Chen; Send security/compliance docs + link to trust center; due: 2025-06-17
Ravi Patel; Create sandbox org + generate expiring API key; due: 2025-06-18
Omar Reyes; Run perf bench using 512-token seq and share CSV; due: 2025-06-20
transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2025-06-15 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi and Jules (Redwood SEs), Laura (Sundial Lead ML Eng), Omar (Sundial DevOps), Priya (PM)

[00:00] Maya: Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining. Can you all hear me?
[00:05] Laura: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:10] Maya: Great. Quick agenda: 1) orient to SDK quickstart in both Python and TypeScript, 2) auth options and sandbox setup, 3) Console + Optimize recommendations for cost/latency, then Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
[00:25] Priya: That works for us, we mainly want to confirm auth and how quickly we can spin up a sandbox for an initial POC.
[00:30] Ravi: Cool. I'll share my screen briefly — showing a small repo with a Python snippet and TS snippet, and then we'll flip to the Console so you can see RBAC and sandbox org settings.

[02:00] (screen share starts)
[02:10] Jules: Starting with Python, here's the gist: install redwood-sdk, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your env, then client = Redwood(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')). There's a generate call, similar to other libs.
[02:30] Omar: Is that a pip package? We run CI in a locked environment — we'd prefer a wheel or private mirror.
[02:40] Ravi: Yes, it's available as a wheel on PyPI; you can vendor it or cache it in your artifact repo. We can also provide an internal installer if you need offline.
[03:05] Laura: And for TypeScript? Our frontend uses Node serverless functions.
[03:15] Jules: TS is the same pattern: npm install @redwood/inference (note: name transcribed, might be different in package.json), set env var REDWOOD_API_KEY, then import Redwood from '@redwood/inference' and call client.chat.create({ messages }) or client.generate. Small differences in method names across SDKs but uniform behavior.
[04:00] Priya: We need SSO — Okta + SAML — for administrative access, anything blocking that?
[04:15] Maya: Not at all. We support SSO with SAML/OIDC for Console access, and you can combine SSO for human users with API-key-based machine credentials.
[04:30] Omar: How do you handle key rotation for long-running services?
[04:40] Ravi: Two options: short-lived keys with automatic refresh via the Console/SDK or use KMS-backed keys. You can also map service principals and rotate keys through our CLI. We'll share the key rotation playbook.

[06:00] (Jules scrolls through Console)
[06:10] Jules: Here's the sandbox org we prepared for demos — you can see a Projects view, API keys page, and RBAC roles. For Sundial we'd typically create a separate org with a few teams: infra, eng, and analytics, each with scoped roles.
[06:45] Laura: Can RBAC limit which models teams can use? We'd like to restrict large-context models to a research group.
[06:55] Jules: Yes, model-level policies are supported. You can define role-based model allowlists, and also set quotas per team to control spend.

[08:00] Priya: On the cost side, what levers do we have — batching, quantization suggestions?
[08:10] Ravi: Exactly — Optimize gives recommendations: batching windows, KV prefix caching, quantized model variants. For embeddings-heavy workloads we suggest using a smaller dimensionality embedding or batched embedding calls to dramatically reduce unit cost.
[08:40] Laura: We're doing semantic search across support tickets — mostly 256–512 token inputs to the embedding model. Any immediate tips?
[08:50] Jules: For that profile: use batching of 32–64 items (depending on latency SLO), and set a warm KV cache for frequent prefixes. Also try 8-bit quantized variants for lower-cost throughput if accuracy impact is acceptable.

[10:00] (demo: quick file in repo)
[10:10] Ravi: I'll run a tiny local script to show a sample generate and an embeddings call. Note: console shows tokens and cost in near-real time.
[10:35] (script output)
[10:40] Omar: The logs show request IDs — can we forward those into our tracing system?
[10:45] Jules: Yes, we provide request_id in response headers and you can attach trace hooks. We also have a tracing integration for Datadog and Tempo — we'll send the integration guide.

[12:30] Laura: About private deployments — if we go Private (VPC/on-prem), what changes? Network, KMS, and audit logs?
[12:45] Maya: Private means you get a customer-managed control plane, options for HSM/KMS integration, and full audit logs. Some features like autoscaling behavior and rollout policies are the same but require additional setup. We'll need to engage infra to confirm bandwidth for model downloads and GPU access.
[13:10] Omar: TL;DR: we prefer hosted sandbox first, then evaluate Dedicated or Private for production.
[13:18] Maya: That's a common path.

[14:00] (brief pause)
[14:10] Priya: Could we see the sample prompt evaluation in Optimize — how regressions are detected?
[14:25] Ravi: Sure — Optimize can run prompt sets over model versions and surface quality drops. I'll open the Optimize tab.
[14:45] (screen shows Optimize dashboard)
[14:50] Jules: Here you can upload labeled prompts and expected outputs; the system will run A/Bs and flag drift. Alerts can be tied to Slack or pager channels.
[15:20] Laura: Nice. Is that part of the hosted plan or an add-on?
[15:28] Maya: Basic Optimize is included; advanced retention and SLA-related evals are an add-on. We'll share the tier doc.

[16:00] Omar: A question on data retention — logs and transcripts for debug — do you store raw prompts by default? We have strict PII rules.
[16:12] Jules: By default, hosted logs are retained but you can opt-out of storing full prompts, mask fields, or use the Private deployment to keep everything in your VPC. We also offer encrypted at-rest and in-transit and can integrate with your KMS.
[16:40] Maya: We'll include the data retention and masking guide in the pack.

[18:00] (Ravi shows a quick TS snippet)
[18:10] Ravi: Example TypeScript snippet: const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-large-v1', messages: [...] }); (note: function names approximate in live transcription)
[19:00] Laura: If we move to dedicated capacity, how long is model provisioning?
[19:10] Jules: For common models, provisioning in Dedicated is usually hours to a day depending on hardware and region. For private on-prem, it's coordination with infra and can be multi-week.

[20:30] Priya: What's the typical SLA and guaranteed latency percentiles?
[20:35] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and target latency. We publish p50/p95 numbers per model in the model catalog; we'll send you the performance profiles for the models you mentioned.

[22:00] (customer dives into infra constraints)
[22:10] Omar: Network egress is limited in our team — will model downloads hit our bandwidth when we escalate?
[22:20] Jules: For Private you host model artifacts — we provide an artifact manager to stream weights. For Dedicated, we handle artifacts but can work with your team to pre-stage to avoid spikes.

[24:00] Laura: For our dev cycle we need ephemeral keys for CI jobs that run in ephemeral containers. Best pattern?
[24:10] Ravi: Use the short-lived keys feature with a refresh token issued by the Console or integrate with your identity provider to mint keys. There's also a CLI to request ephemeral creds that expire in X minutes.

[26:00] (Ravi walks through sample RBAC policy)
[26:10] Jules: Example role: analytics_reader — allowed: embeddings.generate, cannot call model.deploy. Another role: infra_admin — can provision dedicated clusters.

[28:00] (brief cross-talk)
[28:20] Priya: Any gotchas on SDK behavior in cold starts for serverless?
[28:30] Ravi: Cold starts depend on model variant and whether you have warmed KV cache and batch settings. If using serverless, keep batch windows small and pre-warm with a tiny probe. We can share recommended middleware for common serverless frameworks.

[30:00] (Laura asks about demo artifacts)
[30:10] Maya: We linked a sample repo and a quickstart README in the calendar invite (link: https://redwood.example/sundial/quickstart — transcribed link placeholder). Also a benchmark sheet (CSV) and security packet.

[32:00] Omar: We want to run a 1-hour bench: 512 tokens, 50 RPS sustained, compare quantized vs FP16. Can Redwood help run that?
[32:15] Maya: Yes, we can coordinate a short benchmark with our SE team. We'll offer test harness and drop-in scripts.

[34:00] (questions on integrations)
[34:10] Priya: How about secrets rotation — do you integrate with HashiVault?
[34:20] Jules: Yes, HashiCorp Vault is supported for both secrets and KMS integration. We'll attach the Vault example.

[36:00] Laura: Another question: are function call / structured outputs supported in SDKs?
[36:10] Ravi: Yes, SDKs expose function-calling primitives and structured response parsing; some name transcriptions might be slightly off here but the clients do support function annotations and tool calling.

[38:00] (Ravi toggles to Optimize recommendations in Console)
[38:10] Jules: The Optimize tab surfaced a recommended quantization profile for 'redwood-medium-v2' — projected cost cut 30% with <2% accuracy drop on your evals.
[38:40] Laura: Can we try that profile in sandbox first?
[38:45] Maya: Absolutely — we'll enable a canary and give you a toggle in the sandbox so you can A/B.

[40:00] Priya: Any legal / procurement issues — e.g., data residency EU only?
[40:10] Maya: We have EU regions and can ensure data residency; for strict requirements, Private plus on-prem or VPC is recommended. We'll include the regional availability matrix.

[42:00] (wrap-up starts)
[42:10] Maya: Recap: we'll send security pack, provision sandbox org + short-lived API key, give Optimize suggestions and a benchmark harness, and set follow-up POC scoping for week of 6/23.
[42:30] Priya: That sounds good. Laura, anything else?
[42:35] Laura: Please include a sample prompt set for the embedding evals.
[42:40] Maya: Will do.

[44:00] Omar: One last question — support levels for Dedicated: is 24/7 available?
[44:10] Jules: Premium support add-on includes 24/7 on-call and a dedicated TAM. We'll include the support SKU in the pricing doc.

[46:00] (closing notes)
[46:05] Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts. Any blockers on dates for the POC call?
[46:15] Priya: Week of 6/23 works.
[46:20] Laura: Agreed.

[48:00] (meeting ends)

Notes / Artifacts referenced:
- Quickstart repo (Python + TS) — link in calendar (placeholder)
- Security/compliance packet (SOC2 snapshot, data retention, masking guide)
- Sandbox org provisioned for Sundial (pending)
- Benchmark harness (CSV + scripts)

Emissions / Transcription idiosyncrasies: occasional mis-typed package names and function names, proper nouns may be slightly off, timestamps approximate.

End of transcript.
